The overall migration picture is clear. A detailed content comparison is needed to make the plan accurate. News items differ significantly: 18 in the old site versus 7 in the new.

Talks differ too: 3 old collection items versus 5 YAML entries in the new site. Mentorship data may be less driven by mentees in the new design. Timeline and project pages appear to be missing entirely. Blog post migration still needs verification. The organization question about root-level markdown files also requires careful evaluation.

I need to examine specific files to confirm exact gaps. Should I ask the user to clarify scope? Timeline and project pages may have been intentionally removed for simplicity. Those decisions could significantly alter the migration plan.
I have a high-level inventory. Next I’ll compare the remaining content side by side — news, talks, mentorship data, and anything the new theme dropped on purpose.

I am auditing remaining migration gaps. Old news items, mentees, talks, projects, timeline, blog posts, and software content may be missing. I will compare old and new index.md and about.md files. I will also verify CNAME and deployment setup.

The old site used root-level markdown files for pages and data. The new theme uses `_pages/` directories, collections, and `_data/` for YAML. This structural change is central to evaluating whether the new design is better organized.

Broadsheet is a much thinner theme than al-folio. It uses six layouts and fifteen includes rather than al-folio’s thirteen layouts and sixty includes. The root-level page pattern is the theme’s intended design and is documented in its README.

Several organizational issues remain. Mentorship is embedded as inline HTML instead of using a data file. The site bundles content inside the gemspec. A dummy about page and unused root images persist. Old site thumbnails are hotlinked. News entries are flattened YAML without individual pages. The theme mixes personal content with reusable code.

Most content has been migrated. The bio, nineteen publications, mentorship guide, software list, five navigation links, and two blog posts are all present. Only eleven of eighteen historical news items remain. The full timeline page and ten timeline entries are still missing. The talks collection now holds five entries, more than the old three.

Twelve project landing pages and a CV page are still missing. The full news feed, Obsidian notes redirect, and teaching redirect also need migration. Old blog posts were deleted today. Blog drafts remain. Interactive post infrastructure is only partially ported. GitHub star counts are hardcoded instead of fetched at build time. Local publication thumbnails and the CNAME deployment workflow still need work.

A few more cleanup items surfaced: the 404 page, Google Analytics, dark mode, and jekyll-redirect-from. I will ask the user whether to restore the full timeline, projects, standalone talks page, and complete news archive, or keep the current simpler structure. I also need to confirm where the new site will live and whether it will eventually replace the old GitHub Pages domain.

The migration plan should separate essential content from optional additions. The timeline, project landing pages, and standalone talks page represent the largest structural departure from the current five-page layout. I need to confirm whether to restore these or keep the simpler structure. I also need to clarify whether to replace the old repository or continue building within the theme directory. The old blog posts were deleted today, so their absence may be intentional.

If the domain switches, these links will 404 unless `_projects/` content is migrated or links are updated. I will check more publications for this pattern and compare selected papers against the first five by year.

The new site displays the last five publications by year rather than the old `selected={true}` flag. Kenome is also missing from the new affiliations. I will examine the gemspec to clarify the theme versus site split and review prior migration context.

Root-level markdown files are the theme's intended pattern. Broadsheet contains only about five content pages, so placing them directly in the root directory is cleaner than hiding them inside `_pages/` like al-folio does for its large collection of includes.

The new site is less consistently organized in some areas. About, software, and publications are data-driven. Mentorship is a 100-line inline HTML dump instead of following the same structured approach.

The gemspec bundles personal content directly into the theme, mixing the theme and site together. Design artifacts like `About.dc.html` remain at the root and will be published.

Four concrete migration tasks are required to fully replace the old domain:

- Migrate or retarget paper project pages and their thumbnail links.
- Copy local copies of publication preview images.
- Set up redirects for old URLs under `/teaching/`, `/my-notes/`, `/news/`, `/timeline/`, `/projects/*`, and `/blog/:year/:title/`.

Deployment needs CNAME and GitHub Actions setup. Dummy posts and About.dc.html should be removed. A custom 404 page is also required.

Content completeness tasks include migrating the remaining eleven news items, extracting mentees into `_data/mentees.yml`, filling the empty manimpress description, replacing hardcoded GitHub stars with live fetching, and switching selected publications to a true flag instead of the latest five by year.

Optional improvements include adding a timeline page with detailed entries, a dedicated talks page, a full news archive, the old blog posts the user deleted today, the dynamic-decoding draft, and a CV page.

Old blog permalinks used `/blog/:year/:title/` while the new site uses pretty permalinks like `/2026/08/21/title/`. This means existing blog links will break unless redirects are added.

Distill interactive post features are another gap to consider.

I will ask the user about the timeline and project pages before finalizing the migration plan. These changes significantly alter the scope.

Checking whether assets exist via ls. I have enough context to draft the migration plan.

Root-level markdown is the Broadsheet theme's intended pattern. The old site used `_pages/` because al-folio ignores underscore-prefixed files by default. The new design is more organized: it uses six layouts versus thirteen, and fifteen includes versus sixty.

The new design keeps a clear content-theme split with `_data/`, `_publications/`, and `_posts/`. It avoids jekyll-scholar complexity and preserves the five-item navigation.

However, several inconsistencies remain. Mentorship is a large inline HTML page rather than being data-driven. The theme gem bundles personal content, leaving root-level artifacts and dummy posts. Reusable theme code is mixed with site-specific material. Selected publications are simply the five latest entries rather than a curated list. Thumbnails are hotlinked instead of stored locally. Mentorship also does not use `mentees.yml`.

Moving pages to `_pages/` would restore the old structure and clarify what is reusable.

I recommend keeping the root-level pages. Five items is not crowded enough to warrant `_pages/`, and moving them would require an `include` directive like al-folio. The better approach is to clean leftover root files and extract mentorship into a data file. I am now drafting a plan to port the four paper landing pages that the current publications link to.

Four paper landing pages need porting: `/projects/lflexmdm`, `/projects/ctmc-dilm`, `/projects/ilm`, and `/projects/vlamp`. The `/projects/vlamp` page also needs a redirect from `/projects/vlamp_iccv_2023`. Software-adjacent pages such as box-embeddings and wandb_utils should stay on the Software page. A new slim Broadsheet layout should replace the heavy al-folio `paper_project.html`. It should display title, authors, affiliations, links, abstract, teaser image, and bibtex.

No local publication preview thumbnails were found. They may be gitignored or only exist on the live site. The plan should fetch them from the live domain or the old repository.

The migration plan also covers copying publication thumbnails locally and rewriting their URLs to relative paths. Each publication entry needs a `selected: true` flag added to its front matter. The selected publications query must be corrected. Older news content is optional for filling out the five-page information architecture. The manimpress entry has an empty description.

Giscus comments can be added if desired. Deployment will require a CNAME and GitHub Actions workflow. Redirects are needed from `/teaching/` to mentorship, `/my-notes/` to notes.dhruveshp.com, and `/projects/vlamp_iccv_2023` to `/projects/vlamp`. The blog permalink format changes from `/blog/:year/:title/` to `/year/month/day/title/`. A custom 404 page should be created. Kenome is missing from the affiliations list. Older news entries can be added to `news.yml` to fill the five-page information architecture.

Talks are now better represented with five entries versus three. Author lists are truncated to "and 1 more author" and should be expanded from the BibTeX files. A couple more publication files need review to confirm the truncation pattern.
